newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht tumbles, BOT denies devaluation rumour.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht tumbles, BOT denies devaluation rumour.

text.p: The Thai baht tumbled amid new rumours of devaluation but the central bank denied the talk and said it was monitoring the market closely.

"The Bank of Thailand is monitoring the baht market very closely and will take necessary measures to stabilise the value of the baht," Bandid Nijathaworn, director of the BOT's banking department, told Reuters.
"We also wish to deny the rumours in the market about the baht devaluation," he said.
The baht, which was traded at around 25.90 on Thursday, lost nearly 10 satang by late afternoon to 26 per dollar after the offshore attack on the currency.
The baht was bid/offered at 25.950/25.960 at 0937 GMT after the central bank denial of the devaluation rumour.
Dealers said the devaluation rumours were heard in New York and Singapore and had sparked the attacks on the baht, dealers said.

"The attack on the baht was launched because there are people who believe its value should be lower as economic conditions in the country are not as good as they should be," said a senior dealer with a foreign bank.
"It was also aimed at testing the resolve of the Thai central bank in defending the baht," he added.

Dealers also said they believed there were two rounds of BOT intervention in offshore markets to curb the baht's slide in the morning. The BOT was said to have spent up to $800 million defending the currency.
The baht has been dropping against the strengthening U.S. dollar since late last year. The BOT fixed the baht/dollar midrate at 25.87 on Thursday, a 6-1/2 year low.
